Base method for multiplication

Use base 10, then bases in steps of 50: 50, 100, 150, 200, and so on up to 1,000. This set uses two- and three-digit numbers near each base.

1Choose a base. Let each number’s deviation be how far it is above (+) or below (−) the base.
2Find the cross part: first number + second number’s deviation.
3Finish: cross part × base + (deviation 1 × deviation 2).
Base 1012 × 13Cross part 15; deviation product +6 → 15 × 10 + 6 = 156
Base 5048 × 52Cross part 50; deviation product −4 → 50 × 50 − 4 = 2,496
Base 150147 × 154Cross part 151; deviation product −12 → 151 × 150 − 12 = 22,638
Base 1,000997 × 996Cross part 993; deviation product +12 → 993 × 1,000 + 12 = 993,012
Example with two numbers above the base: 104 × 107 using base 100 has deviations +4 and +7. Cross part 111; deviation product +28. So 111 × 100 + 28 = 11,128.

Formulae and identities

Recall each identity before revealing it. Mark whether you remembered it to build a spaced review schedule.

Ia² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)
II(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab
III(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab
IV(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)
V(a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab
VI(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca
VII(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)
VIII(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)
IXa³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)
Xa³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b)
XIa³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)
XIIa³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b)

Multiplication by 11

For a two-digit number, add its digits and place the sum between them. If the sum is 10 or more, carry the 1.

Example · no carry34 × 11 = 3743 | (3 + 4) | 4 → 374
Example · carry58 × 11 = 6385 | (5 + 8) | 8 → carry 1, giving 638
For three digits243 × 11 = 26732 | (2 + 4) | (4 + 3) | 3 → 2 | 6 | 7 | 3 = 2673
